lessons.title: What Latency Actually Means in Trading

children.text: Ask a retail trader what fast means, and they will point to how quickly their broker's app refreshes a live price. Ask a high frequency trading (HFT) desk sitting inside NSE's colocation facility in Mumbai the same question, and the unit of measurement changes completely. Their fast is counted in microseconds, one millionth of a second, and an entire industry exists to shave off a few more of them.

Latency gets used loosely in market commentary, but in trading infrastructure it means three specific, different things. Confusing them is the fastest way to misread a vendor's pitch or a regulator's circular.

markDefs.definition: The full round trip: from a price tick leaving the exchange's dissemination server to the firm's resulting order arriving back at the exchange.

children.text: is the full round trip a strategy ultimately cares about: from the instant a price tick leaves the exchange's dissemination server to the instant the firm's resulting order lands back at the exchange.

markDefs.definition: The time between a firm's server receiving a market data packet and dispatching a responding order. The number most HFT infrastructure teams are actually paid to reduce.

children.text: is the leg engineers spend most of their time optimizing: the time between a firm's server receiving a market data packet and that same server dispatching an order in response to it.

markDefs.definition: The time between an order leaving a firm's server and the exchange's acknowledgment of that order arriving back at the firm.

children.text: is narrower still: just the time between an order leaving the firm's server and the exchange's acknowledgment of that order arriving back.

body.text: One second holds 1,000,000 microseconds. The 10 to 50 microsecond range above is not a rounding error against a retail order's few hundred milliseconds. It is a different universe of speed, and Indian HFT desks pay real money, crores of rupees a year in colocation fees, dedicated fibre and specialised hardware, to live in it.

children.text: Why This Number Is the Entire Business

markDefs.definition: The exchange's matching rule: among orders at the same price, the one that arrived earliest at the matching engine is filled first.

children.text: This is why a firm colocated at NSE will spend crores of rupees a year on rack space, dedicated fibre and specialised hardware to save a few hundred nanoseconds. Exchanges fill orders using

: at a given price, the order that arrives at the matching engine first gets filled first. When Nifty futures on NSE and the underlying cash market both react to the same news, whichever side's order reaches the matching engine microseconds sooner captures the mispricing before it closes. There is no partial credit for arriving second.

body.label: NSE Colocation
body.context: The year exchange-side colocation racks became available to trading members at NSE, moving HFT infrastructure onto Indian soil for the first time.

body.text: In high frequency trading, latency is not overhead to be minimized quietly in the background. It is the product the firm is built to sell.

body.title: Naming the leg
body.question: A firm's server receives a market data packet at 10:15:00.000100 and dispatches its responding order at 10:15:00.000106. What is being measured between these two timestamps?
body.explanation: This is tick-to-trade latency: the gap between the firm's server receiving market data and that same server dispatching an order in response. Wire-to-wire would also include the time for that order to travel back to the exchange, and order-to-ack would start only once the order leaves the server.

body.title: Who gets filled
body.question: Two brokers submit buy orders for the same stock at the same price on NSE. Order A arrives at the matching engine 3 microseconds before Order B. Which order gets filled first, and why?
options: Order B, because larger orders get priority
Order A, because of price-time priority
Neither, the exchange randomizes order matching
Order A, because it is always the first order placed that day
body.explanation: Price-time priority means that among orders resting at the same price, the earliest arrival at the matching engine wins the fill. Order size and time of day do not override this once price is equal.

points: Wire-to-wire, tick-to-trade, and order-to-ack measure three different legs of the same round trip. Know which one a claim is actually about before comparing numbers.
Retail order latency (a few hundred milliseconds) and colocated HFT latency (tens of microseconds) differ by roughly four orders of magnitude.
NSE has offered colocation racks to trading members since 2010, giving firms that pay for rack space physical proximity to the matching engine.
Price-time priority is the reason speed has value at all: the earliest order at a given price wins the fill, with no partial credit for arriving second.
